category: Physics interfaces I: structural mechanics, heat transfer & fluid flow
description: The three classical continuum branches of the COMSOL Model Builder: Solid Mechanics and the structural element interfaces, the Heat Transfer family, and the single-phase and porous-media flow interfaces, together with the material models, constraints, loads, sources and boundary conditions that are added under them. Each entry gives the Add Physics path or right-click path plus the matching COMSOL API for Java calls, where the last integer in create() is the entity dimension (3 = domain in 3D, 2 = boundary in 3D, 1 = edge, 0 = point).

tools.name: Solid Mechanics (solid)
tools.description: Solves the momentum balance of a deformable continuum, -div(sigma) = F_V (plus rho*d2u/dt2 for dynamics), for the displacement vector u and derived stress and strain tensors. Available in 3D, 2D plane stress / plane strain, 2D axisymmetric and 1D, and supports stationary, time dependent, eigenfrequency, frequency domain, prestressed, linear buckling and random vibration studies. Use it for bulk parts where no dimension is negligibly thin; switch to Shell, Plate, Membrane, Beam or Truss when one or two dimensions are much smaller than the rest. Large-deformation behaviour is controlled by the Include geometric nonlinearity checkbox in the study step, not in the interface itself.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Solid Mechanics (solid)

parameters.name: Structural transient behavior
parameters.description: Include inertial terms (Include inertial terms) or treat the transient as quasi-static.

parameters.name: 2D approximation
parameters.description: Plane stress, plane strain or generalized plane strain for 2D components; sets which out-of-plane components are constrained.

parameters.name: Thickness d
parameters.description: Out-of-plane thickness used in 2D to scale loads, mass and stiffness.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Shape-function order for the displacement field: Linear, Quadratic (default), Cubic or Quartic serendipity/Lagrange.

parameters.name: Structural damping
parameters.description: Interface-level default damping model (none, Rayleigh, isotropic loss factor) used by frequency-domain and time-dependent studies.

tools.notes: A linear-elastic Solid Mechanics interface (stationary, time dependent, eigenfrequency) ships with the core COMSOL Multiphysics package; plasticity, creep, hyperelasticity, contact, shells, beams, fatigue and nonlinear material libraries require the Structural Mechanics Module (and the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module for the advanced material models). Every interface carries a default Linear Elastic Material (lemm1), Free boundary condition and Initial Values node.

tools.name: Linear Elastic Material
tools.description: The default domain material model of Solid Mechanics: Hooke's law sigma = C:(epsilon - epsilon_inel) with a linear, optionally anisotropic elasticity tensor C and small-strain kinematics (or a hyperelastic-consistent formulation when geometric nonlinearity is on). It is the node you edit to supply Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio, bulk/shear moduli, Lame parameters or a full elasticity matrix, plus the density used for mass and inertia. Use it for metals, ceramics and any material staying below yield; add subnodes such as Plasticity, Creep, Viscoelasticity, Damping or Thermal Expansion to extend it.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Solid Mechanics (solid) > Linear Elastic Material 1 (present by default), or right-click Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material to add another for a different domain group

parameters.name: Young's modulus E
parameters.description: Elastic stiffness; taken From material by default, or set to User defined.

parameters.name: Poisson's ratio nu
parameters.description: Lateral contraction ratio; nu -> 0.5 makes the material nearly incompressible and usually needs a mixed formulation.

parameters.name: Density rho
parameters.description: Mass density used for inertia, gravity and eigenfrequency analysis.

parameters.name: Solid model
parameters.description: Isotropic, Orthotropic or Anisotropic, and which pair of constants is entered (E and nu, bulk and shear modulus, Lame parameters, pressure-wave and shear-wave speeds).

parameters.name: Use mixed formulation
parameters.description: Adds pressure as an extra dependent variable for (nearly) incompressible materials.

tools.notes: The default tag is lemm1. Leaving the *_mat properties at their default ("from_mat") makes the node read E, nu and rho from the assigned Material node instead, which is the usual practice; the explicit userdef route above is only for one-off overrides. Related nodes: Nonlinear Elastic Material, Hyperelastic Material, Piezoelectric Material, Rigid Material.

tools.name: Hyperelastic Material
tools.description: Domain material model for rubber-like and biological solids in which stress derives from a strain-energy density W(C) rather than a constant stiffness, so the response stays elastic but strongly nonlinear at large strain. COMSOL ships Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin (2, 5 and 9 parameters), Yeoh, Ogden, Arruda-Boyce, Gent, Storakers, Blatz-Ko, Varga, Murnaghan and user-defined strain energy functions, with near-incompressible and fully incompressible mixed formulations. Use it for seals, gaskets, tyres, elastomeric mounts and soft tissue; it always requires geometric nonlinearity, which COMSOL turns on automatically in the study.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Solid Mechanics (solid) > right-click > Material Models > Hyperelastic Material

parameters.name: Material model
parameters.description: Strain-energy form: Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin, Ogden, Yeoh, Arruda-Boyce, Gent, User defined, and others.

parameters.name: Model parameters
parameters.description: The constants of the chosen model, for example mu and kappa (Neo-Hookean) or C10, C01 (Mooney-Rivlin, two parameter).

parameters.name: Compressibility
parameters.description: Compressible, Nearly incompressible with the given isochoric strain energy, or Incompressible (adds a pressure variable).

parameters.name: Density rho
parameters.description: Mass density for dynamic and gravity-loaded analyses.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module (with the Structural Mechanics Module). The API type string for this node is not quoted here on purpose - record the action with File > Save As > Model File for Java (or Compact History) to capture the exact create() type string for your version. Nearly incompressible models mesh best with quadratic displacement and linear pressure discretization.

tools.name: Plasticity
tools.description: Subnode of Linear Elastic Material (or Nonlinear Elastic Material) that adds rate-independent elastoplasticity: an elastic region bounded by a yield function, a flow rule for the plastic strain increment, and a hardening law. Yield criteria include von Mises, Tresca, Hill orthotropic and the porous/soil criteria, with perfectly plastic, isotropic (linear, Ludwik, Swift, Voce, hardening-function) and kinematic hardening. Use it whenever the load takes a metal past yield - forming, crash, bolt preload, low-cycle fatigue - and remember that the solution then depends on load history, so run a parametric or time-dependent ramp rather than a single stationary step.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Solid Mechanics (solid) > Linear Elastic Material 1 > right-click > Plasticity

parameters.name: Yield function F
parameters.description: von Mises stress (default), Tresca stress, Hill orthotropic plasticity or a user-defined function.

parameters.name: Initial yield stress sigma_ys
parameters.description: Stress at which plastic flow begins; read from the material or entered directly.

parameters.name: Isotropic hardening model
parameters.description: Perfectly plastic, Linear (tangent modulus E_Tiso), Ludwik, Swift, Voce, Hockett-Sherby or Hardening function.

parameters.name: Kinematic hardening model
parameters.description: No kinematic hardening, Linear (Prager), Armstrong-Frederick or Chaboche for cyclic loading.

parameters.name: Plasticity model
parameters.description: Small plastic strains or Large plastic strains (multiplicative decomposition) for finite-strain forming problems.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module. Ramp the load in steps (auxiliary sweep or time dependent) so the return-mapping algorithm can follow the load path; a single large step often fails to converge. Related subnodes: Creep, Viscoplasticity, Viscoelasticity, Damage.

tools.name: Fixed Constraint
tools.description: Sets the displacement vector to zero (u = 0) on the selected domains, boundaries, edges or points, i.e. a perfectly rigid, fully clamped support. It is the simplest way to remove the rigid-body modes that otherwise make a stationary structural problem singular. Use it for bolted-down faces and built-in ends; prefer Prescribed Displacement, Roller, Symmetry or a Spring Foundation when the real support is only partly constrained or has finite stiffness, because a Fixed Constraint creates artificial stress concentrations at its edges.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Solid Mechanics (solid) > right-click > Fixed Constraint (also available under Shell, Beam, Truss, Membrane and Multibody Dynamics)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Geometric entities to clamp; entity level is chosen by the create() dimension argument or by the right-click submenu (Domain/Boundary/Edge/Point Constraints).

parameters.name: Apply reaction terms on
parameters.description: All physics (symmetric) or Individual dependent variables - affects how reaction forces are assembled.

parameters.name: Constraint method
parameters.description: Elemental or Nodal constraint enforcement, relevant when constraints overlap or when using weak constraints.

tools.notes: The API type string is "Fixed"; the dimension argument selects the entity level (2 = boundary in 3D, 1 = boundary in 2D or edge in 3D, 0 = point). Reaction forces at the constraint are available as solid.RFx, solid.RFy, solid.RFz and can be summed with a Surface Integration under Results > Derived Values.

tools.name: Prescribed Displacement
tools.description: Imposes a given displacement on selected entities, component by component, so you can fix only x while leaving y and z free, or drive a face by a known stroke u0(t). It is the general form behind Roller (normal component zero), Symmetry and the fixed constraint, and it is the natural way to apply enforced motion in a forming, contact or fatigue model. Use it whenever the kinematics are known and the reaction force is the quantity of interest.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Solid Mechanics (solid) > right-click > Prescribed Displacement (Domain, Boundary, Edge or Point variants)

parameters.name: Prescribed in x / y / z direction
parameters.description: Checkboxes selecting which displacement components are constrained; unchecked components remain free.

parameters.name: u0x, u0y, u0z
parameters.description: Prescribed displacement values, which may be expressions of time, parameters or coordinates (for example "stroke*t/t_end").

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Global or a user-defined/boundary system, so the constraint can be applied along a normal or a rotated axis.

tools.notes: The API type string for Prescribed Displacement differs by entity level and version, so it is shown here as a GUI step - record it with File > Save As > Model File for Java to get the exact string. Related nodes: Prescribed Velocity, Prescribed Acceleration, Roller, Symmetry, Antisymmetry, Rigid Connector.

tools.name: Boundary Load
tools.description: Applies a distributed surface traction to selected boundaries: a load defined per unit area (pressure or traction vector), a total force spread over the selection, or a load per unit deformed/undeformed area for large-strain problems. This is the standard way to enter pressure vessels, wind and hydrostatic loading, bearing pressures and any traction handed over from another physics. Use Body Load for volumetric loads such as gravity or centrifugal force, and Edge Load / Point Load for line and concentrated loads.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Solid Mechanics (solid) > right-click > Boundary Load

parameters.name: Load type
parameters.description: Load defined as force per unit area, Pressure (acts along the inward normal), Total force, or force per unit length in 2D.

parameters.name: FperArea
parameters.description: Traction vector components when the load is given per unit area.

parameters.name: Pressure p
parameters.description: Scalar pressure value when Load type = Pressure; positive p pushes the surface inward.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Global, boundary system or a user-defined system so a follower load can track the deformed normal.

tools.notes: The property name depends on the selected Load type (force per area vs. Pressure vs. Total force), so check the chosen variant when scripting. In a geometrically nonlinear analysis a load entered in the material (undeformed) frame does not rotate with the surface - use the boundary coordinate system or the deformed-area option for a follower load. Volumetric loads go on the companion Body Load node, created the same way with type "BodyLoad" on dimension 3 and a FperVol vector such as {0, 0, -solid.rho*g_const}; for self-weight prefer the Gravity node (which also feeds prestressed and eigenfrequency studies) and for spinning parts the Rotating Frame node, which adds centrifugal, Coriolis and Euler terms.

tools.name: Contact
tools.description: Enforces non-penetration and optional friction between a source and a destination boundary set that are defined as a Contact Pair under Component > Definitions > Pairs. COMSOL offers penalty, augmented Lagrangian and Nitsche formulations, with Coulomb friction, adhesion, decohesion, wear and contact heat/electrical conductance subnodes. Use it for press fits, bolted joints, gaskets, snap fits and any assembly where parts may separate or slide; the analysis is always nonlinear and the geometry must be built as an Assembly (Form Assembly) so that the contacting surfaces keep separate meshes.
tools.usage: First Component 1 > Definitions > right-click Pairs > Contact Pair (pick source and destination boundaries), then Component 1 > Solid Mechanics (solid) > right-click > Pairs > Contact

parameters.name: Contact pair
parameters.description: The Contact Pair defining source (usually the coarser or stiffer surface) and destination boundaries.

parameters.name: Contact method
parameters.description: Penalty, Penalty, dynamic, Augmented Lagrangian or Nitsche; augmented Lagrangian enforces the constraint most accurately but costs extra degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Penalty factor
parameters.description: Contact stiffness, entered directly or from a preset (from material / manual tuning); too low lets surfaces interpenetrate, too high hurts convergence.

parameters.name: Offset from geometric gap
parameters.description: Initial gap or interference used to model a press fit without modelling the interference in the geometry.

parameters.name: Friction (subnode)
parameters.description: Coulomb friction coefficient mu, cohesion sliding resistance and the friction traction penalty.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Always ramp the load or the prescribed displacement (parametric continuation) so contact is established gradually, and refine the destination mesh relative to the source. Related: Contact Pair under Definitions, Friction, Adhesion, Decohesion and Wear subnodes, and the Thermal Contact node in Heat Transfer.

tools.name: Shell (shell)
tools.description: Models thin-walled structures on boundaries (in 3D) or on the boundary of an axisymmetric geometry using a first-order shear-deformation (Mindlin-Reissner) formulation with displacement and rotation degrees of freedom, so bending, membrane and transverse-shear behaviour are all captured without meshing the thickness. Layered composites are supported through a Layered Material and the Composite Materials Module. Use it for sheet metal, pressure-vessel walls, casings and stiffened panels where the thickness is roughly a tenth of the other dimensions or less - a solid mesh of such a part would need an impractical number of elements.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Shell (shell)

parameters.name: Thickness d
parameters.description: Shell thickness, entered in the Thickness and Offset node; can vary by selection or be taken from a Layered Material.

parameters.name: Offset definition
parameters.description: Where the meshed surface sits relative to the physical shell: no offset (mid-surface), top/bottom surface, or user-defined relative offset.

parameters.name: Use MITC interpolation
parameters.description: Mixed interpolation of tensorial components, on by default, to avoid shear locking in thin shells.

parameters.name: Structural transient behavior
parameters.description: Include inertial terms or quasi-static.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Companion element interfaces with the same style of settings: Plate (plate) for 2D flat plates, Membrane (mbrn) for tension-only films with no bending stiffness, Beam (beam) for slender bending members, Truss (truss) for axial-only bars and cables, and Multibody Dynamics (mbd) for assemblies of rigid and flexible bodies joined by hinges, prismatic and other joints. Connect a shell to a solid with the Solid-Thin Structure Connection multiphysics coupling.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Solids (ht)
tools.description: Solves the heat equation rho*Cp*dT/dt + rho*Cp*u.grad(T) = div(k grad T) + Q in solid domains, where conduction dominates and the optional translational term covers moving solids. It is the default member of the Heat Transfer family and carries the Solid domain node, Initial Values and a Thermal Insulation boundary condition by default. Use it for thermal management, heat sinks, electronics cooling of the solid side, heat treatment and any conduction problem; add Fluid, Porous Medium, Biological Tissue or Thin Layer nodes to the same interface to mix in other media.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Heat Transfer in Solids (ht)

parameters.name: Thermal conductivity k
parameters.description: Isotropic, diagonal or full tensor, normally taken From material.

parameters.name: Density rho and Heat capacity Cp
parameters.description: Set the thermal mass rho*Cp that controls transient response.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Shape function order for T; Linear is the default and is usually enough, Quadratic improves accuracy on coarse meshes.

parameters.name: Ambient settings
parameters.description: Interface-level ambient temperature, pressure, humidity and solar irradiance used by radiation and convective-flux nodes.

tools.notes: A core COMSOL Multiphysics capability - the Heat Transfer Module adds surface-to-surface and participating-media radiation, thin layers and shells, moist air, bioheat, phase change and the heat-transfer multiphysics interfaces. Bioheat Transfer is the same ht interface with a Biological Tissue domain node (Pennes perfusion term plus a thermal damage subnode) and is added from Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Bioheat Transfer.

tools.name: Heat Transfer in Fluids
tools.description: The fluid-side variant of the Heat Transfer interface: the same energy equation but with a Fluid domain node that adds the convective term rho*Cp*u.grad(T), pressure work and viscous dissipation, and that reads the velocity field u either from a user expression or from a flow interface. Use it for forced and natural convection, ducts and channels, and as the thermal half of a conjugate heat transfer model. Couple it to Laminar or Turbulent Flow with the Nonisothermal Flow multiphysics node so that density and viscosity follow temperature and the turbulent heat flux is modelled consistently.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Heat Transfer in Fluids, or add a Fluid node under an existing Heat Transfer (ht) interface: Component 1 > Heat Transfer in Solids (ht) > right-click > Fluid

parameters.name: Velocity field u
parameters.description: User defined expression or the velocity of a coupled flow interface (spf.u, spf.v, spf.w).

parameters.name: Absolute pressure pA
parameters.description: Pressure used to evaluate temperature- and pressure-dependent gas properties; normally coupled to the flow interface pressure.

parameters.name: Fluid type
parameters.description: Gas/Liquid, Moist air, or Ideal gas / non-ideal equations of state that set how rho, Cp and gamma are evaluated.

parameters.name: Include viscous dissipation / pressure work
parameters.description: Extra source terms that matter for high-speed or highly viscous flow.

tools.notes: The shortcut Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Conjugate Heat Transfer adds a flow interface, a heat transfer interface and the Nonisothermal Flow coupling in one step. Free convection needs a buoyancy Volume Force (or the Gravity node) in the flow interface and a temperature-dependent density; without it the model will show pure forced convection only.

tools.name: Heat Source
tools.description: Adds a volumetric heat generation term Q (W/m^3) to selected domains, either as a general source, as a total heat rate spread over the selection, or as a linear source q_s*(T_ref - T). Typical uses are Joule losses, exothermic reaction heat, radioactive or metabolic heating, and any power dissipation handed over from another physics as an expression. Boundary and line equivalents exist as Boundary Heat Source, Line Heat Source and Point Heat Source.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Heat Transfer in Solids (ht) > right-click > Heat Source

parameters.name: Q0
parameters.description: Volumetric heat source in W/m^3, which may be any expression, for example ec.Qh for resistive heating.

parameters.name: Heat rate P0
parameters.description: Total power in W distributed uniformly over the selected volume when Heat source = Heat rate.

parameters.name: Linear source q_s
parameters.description: Coefficient of the T-dependent source form q_s*(T_ref - T), useful for lumped convective or reaction terms.

tools.notes: When the source comes from electromagnetics, prefer the Electromagnetic Heating multiphysics coupling over a hand-written Q expression - it also adds the reverse temperature dependence of conductivity. Check the sign convention: Q > 0 heats the domain.

tools.name: Temperature
tools.description: Dirichlet boundary condition that pins the temperature on selected boundaries (or edges/points) to a prescribed value T0, which may be a constant, a parameter, a function of position or a time-dependent ramp. Use it for surfaces held by a thermostat, a large reservoir or a known measured temperature, and as the counterpart to a Heat Flux condition on the rest of the model. Because it supplies whatever heat is needed to hold T0, always check the resulting reaction flux (ht.ntflux) for physical plausibility.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Heat Transfer in Solids (ht) > right-click > Temperature

parameters.name: T0
parameters.description: Prescribed temperature; can reference parameters, functions or the ambient temperature variable ht.Tamb.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Apply reaction terms on all physics or individual variables, and Elemental vs. Nodal constraint method.

tools.notes: Related conditions: Open Boundary (inflow temperature only where flow enters), Inflow (accounts for the upstream enthalpy in a convection problem, usually better than Temperature at a fluid inlet), and Outflow (zero conductive flux). The default exterior condition of the interface is Thermal Insulation, -n.q = 0.

tools.name: Heat Flux
tools.description: Neumann boundary condition supplying a heat flux through selected boundaries. Besides a general inward flux q0, it offers a Convective heat flux form q0 = h*(T_ext - T) with the film coefficient h entered directly or taken from COMSOL's built-in heat-transfer-coefficient correlations (plates, cylinders, spheres, channels, forced or natural convection), and a Heat rate form that spreads a total power over the selection. Use the convective form to close a model at an air-cooled surface without meshing the surrounding fluid.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Heat Transfer in Solids (ht) > right-click > Heat Flux

parameters.name: Flux type
parameters.description: General inward heat flux (q0), Convective heat flux (h and T_ext), or Heat rate (total P0).

parameters.name: q0
parameters.description: Inward flux density in W/m^2; positive values heat the domain.

parameters.name: Heat transfer coefficient h
parameters.description: User defined, or from an External/Internal natural or forced convection correlation with a characteristic length.

parameters.name: External temperature Text
parameters.description: Ambient temperature driving the convective exchange; often set to the interface Ambient temperature.

tools.notes: Convective Heat Flux is a setting of this node in 6.x rather than a separate feature. Combine it with Surface-to-Ambient Radiation on the same boundary when the surface is hot enough for radiation to matter (roughly above 100 C for typical emissivities). The heat-transfer-coefficient correlation library requires the Heat Transfer Module.

tools.name: Surface-to-Ambient Radiation
tools.description: Adds the grey-body radiative flux -n.q = epsilon*sigma*(T_amb^4 - T^4) on selected boundaries, treating the surroundings as a large black enclosure at the ambient temperature. It is far cheaper than a full view-factor calculation and is the right choice when the radiating surface does not see itself or other parts of the model. Use it on external casings, fins and any hot surface radiating to a room; switch to the Surface-to-Surface Radiation interface when reflections and shadowing between surfaces matter.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Heat Transfer in Solids (ht) > right-click > Surface-to-Ambient Radiation

parameters.name: Surface emissivity epsilon
parameters.description: Between 0 and 1, from the material library or user defined; may be wavelength-dependent when spectral bands are used.

parameters.name: Ambient temperature Tamb
parameters.description: Temperature of the notional surroundings; can reference the interface-level Ambient settings.

parameters.name: Stefan-Boltzmann constant
parameters.description: Taken from the built-in physical constants by default.

tools.notes: This node stacks additively with Heat Flux on the same boundary. Because the term is quartic in T, always solve in absolute temperature units and give a sensible initial value; a poor initial guess is the usual cause of a failed stationary solve. The related Thin Layer node models a thermally resistive or highly conductive coating on a boundary without meshing it.

tools.name: Surface-to-Surface Radiation (rad)
tools.description: Computes radiative exchange inside an enclosure by solving for the surface radiosity with view factors obtained from hemicube, ray-shooting or direct-area integration, so reflections, shadowing and partial enclosures are handled. It can be used alone or, far more commonly, coupled to a Heat Transfer interface through the Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation multiphysics interface. Use it for furnaces, solar collectors, spacecraft thermal control, LED and lamp housings and any cavity where surfaces radiate at each other; add spectral bands for wavelength-dependent emissivity and a Solar radiation source for external irradiation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Radiation > Surface-to-Surface Radiation (rad), or Heat Transfer > Heat Transfer with Surface-to-Surface Radiation to get the coupled pair

parameters.name: Radiation resolution
parameters.description: Number of rays / hemicube resolution used for the view-factor computation; higher is more accurate and much slower.

parameters.name: Surface-to-surface radiation method
parameters.description: Hemicube, Direct area integration or Ray shooting - direct area integration ignores shadowing, so use hemicube or ray shooting for concave enclosures.

parameters.name: Wavelength dependence of emissivity
parameters.description: Constant, Solar and ambient (two bands) or Multiple spectral bands.

parameters.name: Diffuse Surface / Diffuse Mirror
parameters.description: Boundary nodes giving emissivity and ambient irradiation; Diffuse Mirror is a perfectly reflecting (epsilon = 0) surface.

tools.notes: Requires the Heat Transfer Module. The view-factor computation dominates the cost and scales badly with the number of radiating elements, so keep the radiating mesh coarse and use symmetry planes. For media that absorb, emit and scatter (combustion gases, glass, semi-transparent insulation) use Radiation in Participating Media instead, which solves the radiative transfer equation with discrete ordinates or P1 approximation.

tools.name: Laminar Flow (spf)
tools.description: Solves the Navier-Stokes equations rho*(du/dt + u.grad(u)) = div(-pI + K) + F together with the continuity equation for the velocity field u and pressure p, in compressible (Ma < 0.3), weakly compressible or incompressible form. It carries a Fluid Properties domain node, a no-slip Wall condition on all exterior boundaries and an Initial Values node by default. Use it whenever the Reynolds number is low enough that the flow stays laminar - microfluidics, polymer and oil flow, small channels, low-speed external flow; use Creeping Flow (the same interface with the inertial term dropped) for Re much less than 1, and a Turbulent Flow interface above the transition.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Laminar Flow (spf)

parameters.name: Compressibility
parameters.description: Incompressible flow, Weakly compressible flow (density from temperature only) or Compressible flow (Ma < 0.3).

parameters.name: Neglect inertial term (Stokes flow)
parameters.description: Drops rho*u.grad(u), turning the interface into Creeping Flow for very low Reynolds numbers.

parameters.name: Turbulence model type
parameters.description: None for laminar; switching it here is equivalent to picking one of the Turbulent Flow interfaces.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: P1+P1 with streamline/crosswind stabilization (default, cheap) or P2+P1 Taylor-Hood for higher accuracy.

parameters.name: Enable porous media domains
parameters.description: Allows Porous Medium (Brinkman) domain nodes inside the same interface.

tools.notes: Single-phase flow ships in the core package in a basic form; the CFD Module, Microfluidics Module, Polymer Flow Module and Porous Media Flow Module add turbulence models, multiphase flow, non-Newtonian rheology and porous domains. Check the Reynolds number in Results before trusting a laminar solution, and always set a pressure level (an Outlet with p = 0 or a Pressure Point Constraint) or the problem is singular.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, k-epsilon (spf)
tools.description: Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes interface that closes the Reynolds stresses with the standard two-equation k-epsilon model, adding transport equations for turbulent kinetic energy k and its dissipation rate epsilon and an eddy viscosity mu_T = rho*C_mu*k^2/epsilon. It uses wall functions by default, so the first mesh layer may sit in the log layer and the mesh stays affordable. Use it as the default workhorse for high-Reynolds internal flows, ducts, mixers and heat exchangers where the boundary layer itself is not the quantity of interest.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, k-epsilon (spf)

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: Switchable on the interface: k-epsilon, Realizable k-epsilon, k-omega, SST, Low Reynolds number k-epsilon, Spalart-Allmaras, v2-f, Algebraic yPlus or L-VEL.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Wall functions, Automatic (blends wall functions and low-Re resolution) or Low Re, which needs y+ of order 1 at the wall.

parameters.name: Turbulence intensity IT and length scale LT
parameters.description: Inlet boundary values that set the incoming k and epsilon.

parameters.name: Use pseudo time stepping
parameters.description: On by default for stationary turbulent solves; greatly improves robustness from a poor initial guess.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (also available with the Heat Transfer Module for nonisothermal flow). All turbulent single-phase interfaces use the default tag spf, so only one of them can keep that tag in a component. Model choice: k-epsilon is robust but poor in strong adverse pressure gradients and separation; SST resolves boundary layers better but needs a wall-resolved mesh; Low Reynolds number k-epsilon is for transition and wall heat flux accuracy. Verify spf.yPlus after solving to check that the wall treatment assumption holds.

tools.name: Inlet
tools.description: Specifies how fluid enters the domain: a normal inflow velocity, a full velocity vector, a fully developed (laminar or turbulent) inflow profile computed on the fly, an inlet pressure, or a mass flow rate. The fully developed option solves an auxiliary problem on the boundary so you can start the model at the real inlet plane instead of extending the channel upstream. Use it on every boundary where flow enters; combine with an Outlet somewhere else in the model so the pressure level is defined.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Laminar Flow (spf) > right-click > Inlet

parameters.name: Boundary condition
parameters.description: Velocity, Fully developed flow, Pressure, Mass flow or Displaced mesh velocity.

parameters.name: Velocity field u0 / normal inflow velocity U0in
parameters.description: The prescribed velocity vector or the magnitude of the inward normal velocity.

parameters.name: Pressure p0
parameters.description: Inlet pressure when Boundary condition = Pressure; can suppress backflow with the Suppress backflow option.

parameters.name: Average velocity / Flow rate / Average pressure
parameters.description: Entry quantity for a fully developed inflow, which COMSOL turns into the matching parabolic or turbulent profile.

parameters.name: Turbulence conditions
parameters.description: Turbulent intensity and length scale (or explicit k and epsilon/omega) when a turbulence model is active.

tools.notes: The property that holds the entered value depends on the chosen Boundary condition (normal velocity, velocity vector, pressure, mass flow), so check the variant when scripting. A pressure inlet combined with a pressure outlet leaves the flow rate as an unknown and is much harder to converge than a velocity inlet.

tools.name: Outlet
tools.description: Defines where fluid leaves: normally a prescribed static pressure (often 0 as a reference level), but also velocity, mass flow or a fully developed outflow that lets the profile adjust itself. The Normal flow option forces the velocity to be perpendicular to the boundary, and Suppress backflow adds a penalty that prevents unphysical reverse flow on a recirculating outlet. Use exactly one pressure-type condition somewhere in an incompressible model to pin the pressure level; otherwise the pressure is determined only up to a constant.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Laminar Flow (spf) > right-click > Outlet

parameters.name: Boundary condition
parameters.description: Pressure, Velocity, Fully developed flow or Mass flow.

parameters.name: Pressure p0
parameters.description: Static pressure at the outlet; 0 is the usual gauge reference.

parameters.name: Normal flow
parameters.description: Constrains the tangential velocity to zero at the outlet.

parameters.name: Suppress backflow
parameters.description: Adjusts the pressure so that no fluid enters through the outlet; on by default and very helpful for recirculating flows.

tools.notes: Place the outlet far enough downstream that the flow is close to developed, or strong gradients at the boundary will pollute the solution upstream. If both inlet and outlet prescribe pressure, add a good initial guess and consider a Pressure Point Constraint for robustness.

tools.name: Wall
tools.description: Default exterior boundary condition of every single-phase flow interface, imposing no slip (u = 0) on a stationary solid surface. Other wall conditions available from the same node are slip (free-slip, u.n = 0), moving wall (a prescribed sliding or translating surface), leaking wall, navier slip and, in turbulent models, the wall function or automatic wall treatment that bridges the unresolved boundary layer. Use Slip on a symmetry-like surface where the boundary layer is not of interest, and Moving Wall for rotating machinery or belt-driven flows.
tools.usage: Present by default as Component 1 > Laminar Flow (spf) > Wall 1; add extra ones with right-click > Wall to give different surfaces different conditions

parameters.name: Boundary condition
parameters.description: No slip, Slip, Navier slip, Leaking wall, Moving wall, Slip velocity, or Wall functions / Automatic wall treatment for turbulence.

parameters.name: Wall movement
parameters.description: Translational velocity of the wall, sliding wall velocity, or velocity of the moving mesh frame.

parameters.name: Apply slip condition on / Constraint settings
parameters.description: Controls how the condition is enforced when it overlaps other constraints at edges and corners.

parameters.name: Roughness
parameters.description: Equivalent sand roughness height used by the turbulent wall functions.

tools.notes: The default wall node (tag wallbc1) has an all-boundaries selection that shrinks automatically as Inlet, Outlet and Symmetry nodes take boundaries over; later wall nodes override earlier ones. For turbulent models inspect spf.yPlus and the Wall Resolution plot to confirm the mesh matches the chosen wall treatment.

tools.name: Volume Force
tools.description: Adds a body force density F (N/m^3) to the momentum equation on selected domains. Its most common use is buoyancy for natural convection, F = rho(T)*g or the Boussinesq form -rho0*alpha*(T - T0)*g, but it also carries Lorentz forces from an electromagnetic interface, porous-media drag written by hand, and magnetohydrodynamic or electrohydrodynamic terms. Use the dedicated Gravity node when you want a hydrostatic-pressure-consistent formulation with a reduced pressure variable.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Laminar Flow (spf) > right-click > Volume Force

parameters.name: F
parameters.description: Force-per-volume vector, for example {0, 0, -spf.rho*g_const} for buoyancy with a temperature-dependent density.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains where the force acts; usually the whole fluid region.

tools.notes: For natural convection also switch the fluid Compressibility to Weakly compressible (or use a temperature-dependent density from the material) - with a constant density the buoyancy term is a constant and produces no flow. The companion Initial Values node sets the starting u and p and is worth giving a sensible non-zero guess in stationary turbulent runs.

tools.name: Darcy's Law (dl)
tools.description: Solves the continuity equation with Darcy's law u = -(kappa/mu)*grad(p), giving the pressure field in a porous medium where viscous drag on the pore walls dominates and inertia is negligible (pore Reynolds number below about 1). Storage, gravity, sources and sinks and unsaturated (Richards) flow are all available as nodes. Use it for groundwater and reservoir flow, filtration, drying, fuel cells and packed beds; move to Brinkman Equations (br) when the velocity is high enough that shear inside the porous matrix matters, and to Free and Porous Media Flow, Brinkman (fp) when an open channel is coupled to a porous region.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Darcy's Law (dl)

parameters.name: Permeability kappa
parameters.description: Isotropic or tensor permeability of the porous matrix, usually from a Porous Material.

parameters.name: Porosity epsilon_p
parameters.description: Void fraction, used by storage, transport coupling and the average velocity.

parameters.name: Dynamic viscosity mu
parameters.description: Fluid viscosity; taken from the fluid material.

parameters.name: Storage model
parameters.description: Linear storage, compressible fluid or user defined, which sets the transient term S*dp/dt.

parameters.name: Mass Flux / Pressure / Inlet / Outlet / No Flow
parameters.description: Boundary nodes; No Flow is the default exterior condition.

tools.notes: Available with the Porous Media Flow Module, the Subsurface Flow Module, the CFD Module, the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module and the Battery Design Module. Couple it to Transport of Diluted Species in Porous Media for solute transport, or to Heat Transfer in Porous Media for non-isothermal subsurface problems. Related interfaces: Brinkman Equations (br), Free and Porous Media Flow, Brinkman (fp), Fracture Flow, Pipe Flow (pfl).

tools.name: Two-Phase Flow, Level Set
tools.description: Multiphysics interface that pairs a single-phase flow interface with a Level Set (ls) interface and a Two-Phase Flow, Level Set coupling node, tracking a sharp fluid-fluid interface as the 0.5 contour of a smoothed level set function phi. The coupling turns phi into the local density and viscosity and adds surface tension as a force concentrated on the interface. Use it for free-surface, droplet, bubble, jet-breakup, filling and mould-injection problems; choose the Phase Field variant instead when the interface topology changes violently or when mass conservation over long times is critical.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Two-Phase Flow, Level Set > Laminar Two-Phase Flow, Level Set (adds spf, ls and the coupling in one step)

parameters.name: Reinitialization parameter gamma
parameters.description: Controls how strongly the level set function is kept as a smooth step; typically the maximum expected velocity magnitude.

parameters.name: Interface thickness epsilon_ls
parameters.description: Half the numerical interface width, usually the typical mesh size in the interface region (ls.hmax/2).

parameters.name: Surface tension coefficient sigma
parameters.description: From the built-in library of fluid pairs or user defined.

parameters.name: Initial Interface / Initial Values
parameters.description: Boundary node setting where the interface starts and which side is fluid 1 vs fluid 2.

parameters.name: Wetted Wall
parameters.description: Wall condition that sets the contact angle and slip length where the interface touches a solid.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or the Microfluidics Module. The standard workflow uses a two-step study: a Phase Initialization step that solves for the distance function, then a Time Dependent step. Keep the mesh uniform and fine across the whole region the interface will travel through; a coarse cell smears the interface and loses mass. Related: Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field, Three-Phase Flow, and the Mixture Model, Bubbly Flow and Euler-Euler interfaces for dispersed multiphase flow.
